property_summary: On a fresh C, lockInGuess succeeds exactly when msg.value is 1 ether, and then C's balance increases by exactly that amount.
After a successful lockInGuess, any further lockInGuess call reverts, even with exactly 1 ether.
settle() always reverts in the same block as lockInGuess (before the target block), and leaves C's balance unchanged.
On a fresh C, lockInGuess reverts whenever the attached value is not exactly 1 ether, leaving C's balance unchanged.
Calling settle() before any lock-in exists always reverts and leaves C's Ether balance unchanged.
Calling settle on a fresh C (no guess locked in) always reverts, regardless of inputs.

property_summary: lockInGuess always reverts and leaves C's balance unchanged unless exactly 1 ether is sent and no guess is already locked in.
After locking a wrong guess and settling, C's balance is unchanged and the user may lock a new guess (settle resets the guess slot).
Calling settle in the same block as lockInGuess always reverts and leaves C's balance unchanged, because settling is only allowed after the target block has passed.

If a user locks the guess keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes32(0))) (the blockhash of a not-yet-mined block) and then calls settle, settle succeeds, pays out exactly 2 ether, and resets the guess slot so no Ether beyond that is transferred.

property_summary: Calling settle() before any guess (or before the guessed block has passed) reverts, and lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether succeeds once and makes settle still revert until a later block.
After a guess is locked in, a second lockInGuess by the same address reverts even with exactly 1 ether, and the contract balance stays at 2 ether.
lockInGuess with an amount other than exactly 1 ether always reverts and leaves the contract's balance unchanged.
A successful lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether increases the contract's balance by exactly 1 ether (from 1 to 2 ether) and does not revert.
After locking a valid guess, settle() always reverts when called in the same transaction because the guessed block has not yet passed, and the contract balance is unchanged.
After lockInGuess, settle always reverts because block.number cannot yet exceed the locked block (block.number+1).
Calling settle() without a locked-in guess always reverts and does not transfer any Ether out of the contract.
